- scripts/review_merge_train.sh:481 | severity=high | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna]
  PROBLEM: A review run transitioning from `in_progress` to `waiting` between the sequential status queries is absent from both results.
  WHY: The missing run key lets `_mt_release` treat the queued PR as having no active review and dispatch a duplicate review; all three reporting reviewers rate this MAJOR.
- tests/test_review_merge_train.py:jq pipeline inside the `actions/runs` fake handler (`... | map(select($cm == "" or ((.created_at // "") != "" and .created_at <= $cm))) as $r ...`) | severity=low | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: The fake handler compares `created_at` timestamps lexicographically, which can misorder timestamps across day or month boundaries.
  WHY: A future bounded-query test spanning such a boundary could produce results unlike the live API; z-ai_glm-5_2 disputed this as a false positive because fixed-width ISO 8601 UTC timestamps sort chronologically.
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- scripts/review_merge_train.sh:481 | severity=high | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The sequential status queries run `waiting` before `in_progress`, so a run transitioning between those statuses can be absent from both results.
  WHY: `_mt_release` can then treat the queued PR as having no active review and dispatch a second review.
- TASK_GAP
  Requirement: The completed plan document (docs/completed/issue-5443-merge-train-complete-run-listing-plan.md) should describe the code as shipped, not only the original plan. AD-12 superseded AD-6, changing the listing from three statuses to five and from 3 calls to 5 calls per invocation.
  Expected change site: docs/completed/issue-5443-merge-train-complete-run-listing-plan.md, the Approach section (line 48, "reads the three active statuses"), Constraints §15 (line 41, "3 calls per release invocation"), the code snippet (lines 50-53, shows three statuses), and Risks & Mitigations (lines 96-97, "three queries", "3 when something is").
  Evidence of absence: Line 48 reads "reads the three active statuses in lifecycle order (pending, queued, in_progress)" and the code snippet at lines 50-53 shows an unfiltered query that the actual code no longer uses. Line 41 says "3 calls per release invocation in the normal case" where the code makes 5 calls. Lines 96-97 say "Runs change status while the three queries run" and "3 when something is [queued]". The progress log documents the evolution, but readers referencing the plan alone see stale counts and an obsolete approach description.
  severity=NIT
  confidence=3

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- scripts/review_merge_train.sh:the `for __mt_runs_status in requested pending queued waiting in_progress; do` loop in `_mt_inflight_review_branches` (the body of the function rewritten in this PR) | severity=high | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The five sequential status queries run `waiting` before `in_progress`; a run transitioning from `in_progress` to `waiting` between those queries is absent from both results.
  WHY: `_mt_release` finds no active review for the queued PR, retires the queue marker, and dispatches a duplicate review; the report says the regression risk is uncaught by tests.
- tests/test_review_merge_train.py:jq pipeline inside the `actions/runs` fake handler (`... | map(select($cm == "" or ((.created_at // "") != "" and .created_at <= $cm))) as $r ...`) | severity=low | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The fake handler compares ISO 8601 `created_at` values lexicographically, which can misorder them across a day or month boundary.
  WHY: A future bounded-query test straddling midnight could silently drop or include the wrong runs, although the reviewer reports that current tests do not cross a day boundary.
- TASK_GAP
  Requirement: The completed plan document and the changelog fragment must agree with the shipped behavior. After AD-12 superseded AD-6, the listing reads five non-terminal statuses (`requested`, `pending`, `queued`, `waiting`, `in_progress`) and normally costs five API calls per release invocation, not three.
  Expected change site: `docs/completed/issue-5443-merge-train-complete-run-listing-plan.md` — `Approach`, `Risks & Mitigations`, and `Constraints`/`§15` reference text (e.g. the `gh_retry gh api ...` snippet, "3 calls per release invocation in the normal case", "3 when something is [queued]" / "Lazy fetch: 0 calls when nothing is queued (previously 1), 3 when something is").
  Evidence of absence: The PR description was updated in the LAST RUN to call out five statuses and five calls, and the changelog row "API calls per release with a queued PR | 5 (one page per status), up from 1" was rewritten, but `docs/completed/issue-5443-merge-train-complete-run-listing-plan.md` still references the three-status loop from AD-6 verbatim: the code snippet still shows `for __mt_runs_status in pending queued in_progress; do`, the Approach narrative still reads "reads the three active statuses in lifecycle order (pending, queued, in_progress)", `§15` still says "3 calls per release invocation in the normal case", and Risks & Mitigations still say "Lazy fetch: 0 calls when nothing is queued (previously 1), 3 when something is." A reader consulting the plan instead of the README row sees stale cycle-count claims. The progress log already records AD-12 and the evolution in its `## Auto-decisions` section, so the information exists — it just never propagated to the plan. The plan moved to `docs/completed/` in completion PR #5696, so this is the version that ships.
  severity=NIT
  confidence=3
=== END FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
